description: Sync cards and their comments from the Guru collections you choose. With Enforce ACL on, the Guru groups that can open a collection decide who can find its cards.
opening: Sync the cards in the Guru collections you select. Each card is one document with its text, collection, verification state and owner. Each comment and each reply is its own document, linked to its card or thread. Attached files can be downloaded and their text added to the card.

The Guru groups that can open a collection restrict search when Enforce ACL is on. Private cards are skipped unless you turn on `include_private_cards`. Tags, folders and verifiers are kept but are not searchable. Cards and comments deleted in Guru stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: A card can be read by the members of the Guru groups that can open its collection. A collection open to All Members or All Organization Members can be read by everyone who can query the collection. A private card, synced only when `include_private_cards` is on, can be read by its owner and its collaborators. A comment follows its card.
permissions.identity: A member's email address. Guru groups are turned into their active members' email addresses.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a collection's group access, or a private card's owner and collaborators, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: Reading a collection's group access needs the user token of a Guru Admin or of the collection's owner. A collection token cannot read it.
Guru Admins are not added to a collection's readers.
A group or audience too large to read in full counts as unreadable.

connect.auth: Guru uses an API token, paired with either your Guru username for a user token, or a collection id for a collection token. Set exactly one of `email` and `collection_id`. The token reads as the user who generated it.

credentials.name: email
credentials.text: Your Guru username, usually your email.

credentials.name: api_token
credentials.text: A Guru collection token. It is read-only and covers one collection, and it cannot read who can open the collection.

credentials.name: collection_id
credentials.text: The id of the token's collection.

settings.name: include_private_cards
settings.text: Set to `true` to also sync private cards, each readable only by its owner and collaborators. Off by default.

permissions.name: Read access to each collection
permissions.text: required. Cards in collections the user cannot open are never synced.

permissions.name: Manage Apps & Integrations
permissions.text: required to generate the token. An Admin can generate it on behalf of the syncing user.

permissions.name: Admin or Collection Owner
permissions.text: optional, for search that follows Guru permissions. Reads which groups can open each collection.

steps.title: Generate a token
steps.text: In Guru, open Manage, Apps & Integrations, API Access and generate a user token, or a collection token for a single collection. For search that follows Guru permissions, use the user token of a Guru Admin or of each collection's owner.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the token as `api_token`. For a user token, add your Guru username as `email`. For a collection token, add the collection id as `collection_id`. To sync private cards, set `include_private_cards` to `true`.

steps.title: Select collections
steps.text: HydraDB lists the collections the token can read. Select the collections to sync. To reach cards older than 30 days, raise `lookback_days` when you select them.

connect.account: One connector reads what one Guru user, or one collection token, can open.

sync.first_sync: Each selected collection reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the cards that were edited, verified or commented on since the last sync. Each card's comments are sent again as their own documents.
sync.edits: An edited card is read again and replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted cards are not removed. A card, comment or reply deleted in Guru stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: If Guru refuses a card's comment list, a change to its comments only can be missed until the card changes again.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the card or comment was last modified, written as the `Updated` line. A card's result date is the later of this and its last verification. A comment's is the later of this and its creation time.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.guru_card_id
shared_attributes.text: The card id. On a card, picks out that card. On a comment, the card it is on, so one key finds a card and its comments. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
shared_attributes.text: The collection id. Limits a query to one collection's cards and comments. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
shared_attributes.text: The collection name. Limits a query to one collection by name. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's cards and comments. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Collection access
shared_attributes.text: The Guru groups that can open the card's collection. For a private card, its owner and collaborators instead. A comment uses its card's. Decides who can read the item when Enforce ACL is on. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: acl_warning
shared_attributes.text: Set when a private card's owner and collaborators could not be read. Explains the missing permissions.

documents.name: Cards
documents.title: The card title. A card with no title is titled `Guru card` and its id.
documents.text: The card content with HTML removed. Plain text and Markdown pass through. If the content has no readable text, the title stands in. The title, author and last-modified time are searchable too.
documents.date: The later of when the card was last modified and when it was last verified, so a re-verified card counts as recent.
documents.files: Attached files can be downloaded and their text added to the card. A file over 25 MiB, of an unsupported type, or that fails to download keeps only its name.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The card owner's display name, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the card as written by its owner.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The card owner's name or email, the same person as `created_by`.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The owner's email. Gives the author an email in the graph, so the same person is recognised across tools. Not searchable.

attributes.name: last_verified
attributes.text: When the card was last verified. When it is later than the last edit, it sets the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.verification_state
attributes.text: The card's trust status, such as `TRUSTED` or `STALE`. Limits a query to trusted cards, or finds stale ones. Not searchable.

attributes.name: share_status
attributes.text: `TEAM`, `PRIVATE` or `PUBLIC`. Private cards are skipped, or with `include_private_cards` on, readable only by their owner and collaborators. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the card was created.

attributes.name: verification_reason
attributes.text: Guru's reason for the verification state, when there is one.

attributes.name: verification_interval
attributes.text: How many days pass between required verifications.

attributes.name: verifiers
attributes.text: The people and groups responsible for verifying the card. Not attached as people in the graph.

attributes.name: verifier_emails
attributes.text: The verifiers' emails. They do not decide who can read the card.

attributes.name: last_verified_by
attributes.text: The name of whoever last verified the card.

attributes.name: last_verified_by_email
attributes.text: That verifier's email.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.text: The last editor's name or email. Not attached as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.text: The last editor's display name.

attributes.name: updated_by_email
attributes.text: The last editor's email.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.text: The card's tag names. A query cannot match or filter on them.

attributes.name: folders
attributes.text: The names of the folders the card is in. A query cannot match or filter on them.

attributes.name: comment_count
attributes.text: How many comments Guru reports for the card.

attributes.name: attachments
attributes.text: The file names of the card's attachments.

documents.name: Comments
documents.one_document: One comment that starts a thread on a card, or one reply in a thread. Empty comments are skipped, except a thread opener whose replies have text.
documents.title: `Comment by` the author's name `on` the card title, or `Comment on` the card title.
documents.text: The comment text with markup removed, with `Author`, `Parent`, `Created` and `Updated` lines.
documents.date: The later of when the comment was created and last modified.
documents.link_back: Opens the card the comment is on.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The comment author as name and email, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the comment as written by that person.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The card for a thread opener, or the thread for a reply, written as the `Parent` line. Links the comment to it.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the comment was created, written as the `Created` line.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.guru_comment_id
attributes.text: The comment id. Picks out one comment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: properties
attributes.text: The comment's status.

example_searches: What does our Guru card say about the refund policy for annual plans?
Which trusted cards in the Sales collection cover competitor pricing?
What did people comment on the onboarding checklist card?

connections: A comment that starts a thread to its card.
No links to items in other tools.
people: The owner of each card, with name and email.
The author of each comment and reply.
Verifiers and editors are kept with the card but not attached as people.
graph.from_text: The card text, the text read from attached files, and the comment text.

not_synced: Cards not edited, verified or commented on within the `lookback_days` window on the first sync.
Collections the token's user cannot open.
Deletions: deleted cards, comments and replies stay in HydraDB.
